//: The pull-request jobs scripts/ci/affected_jobs.py routes by the cmux-tui crate graph: a job runs when the change
touches an input of one of its crates (the crate, every crate it reaches by path dependency with the features
its build turns on, the files their sources name outside them) or one of its own inputs (a path; one ending in
/ is a directory). A workflow's `inputs` are inputs of each of its jobs. `features` are the job's --features;
a `compile_only` job runs no test, so the fixtures its crates' tests read at run time are not its inputs; a
`binaries_only` job uses only its crates' libraries and binaries, so their tests, benches and examples are not.
A change to this file or the router runs every job; so do pushes, dispatches and the full-ci label.
A job another router decides names that router's output (`router_output`): cmux-next.yml's daemon-test reads
scripts/ci/cmux_next_route.py's `daemon`, which takes the job's inputs from here. `binaries_key` is the
reuse-key file of the binaries a job fetches instead of building: each key input outside the crate graph is one
of the job's inputs or a file a cmux-tui Rust source names (the graph places it). `routed_elsewhere` are scripts
its steps run that its router routes by another rule: the generated-files checks it hosts, the package build's
web bundles, and CI plumbing (caches, scratch, checkout repair) the router sends to the checks tier. `key_only` are key inputs no fetched binary reads (fixtures of crate tests and
benches): the key holds them so the published tree is rebuilt, and the job's result cannot change with them.
The replay of the last merged pull requests into feat-cmux-next (cmux PR bodies: the table). Tier A: jobs whose
reds there were never the pull request's own change (base reds, flakes, runner and queue failures). Tier B: jobs
that hid a few (the value names them), fixed forward on the push. All are in workflows a feat-cmux-next push runs.
A pull request skips them unless it carries the full-ci label; the push that lands it runs them, and a red there
names the pull requests in its range. affected_jobs.py check: the job's if: carries PR_SKIP_IF, a push starts its
workflow on every path a pull request does, and nothing that needs it is skipped with it.
